_doc: Sources the book engages with — prior-art books, papers, posts, talks, and the academic PDFs staged for extraction. Each source has at most one primary author (use `coauthors` for additional). `engagement` describes the book's stance toward the source. `representedBy` (optional) links to a Note that materially holds the source (e.g. a conversation transcript that doubles as a Note). `file` (optional) is the staged PDF filename. `availability` is one of: `open` (cleared to commit — file lives in content/sources/), `restricted` (in-copyright — file lives in the gitignored sources-local/, never committed or published), `unverified` (committed but licence not yet confirmed), `external` (no file held — cited by reference only). `tags` is a controlled vocabulary for navigation: `prior-art` (a work the book is in dialogue with), `adversary` (prior art that actively challenges the book's thesis), `evidence` (a source that backs or pressure-tests Claims), `internal` (the author's own corpus), `model-origin` (the source of a model or framing the book adapts).

sources.label: The Democratization Paradox
sources.author: corey-petty
sources.summary: Covers the barriers/volume angle: curation layer, cost-shifting, creation-cheap/review-expensive, inverted-U relationship.
sources.engagement: primary internal source the book draws from

sources.label: The Anatomy of Exposure: How Blockchain Transactions Leak Information at Every Layer
sources.author: corey-petty
sources.summary: Walks a blockchain transaction's full lifecycle — coordination, construction, signing, submission, propagation, inclusion, post-inclusion surveillance, downstream data economy — cataloguing what leaks at each stage and to whom. Supplies Ch 10's transparent-money evidence: IP-to-address correlation as the foundational leak, mempool archives, builder concentration, censorship-by-identifiable-operator, and the analytics industry that monetizes the permanent record.
sources.engagement: primary internal source; the empirical backbone of Ch 10's transparent-money section

sources.label: The Double-Edged Sword of Deep Expertise
sources.author: corey-petty
sources.summary: Working out cross-domain intuition: chunking and deep structural analogies as the cognitive substrate of expert transfer; the four 'curse of expertise' failure modes (paradigm lock-in, overconfidence in cross-application, perceptual filtering, conceptual rigidity); and the prescription for cultivating versatile expertise. Claude-assisted.
sources.engagement: primary internal source — supplies Chapter 9's bridge-node mechanism

sources.label: General Theme (conversation transcript)
sources.author: corey-petty
sources.summary: Conversation transcript where the book concept got laid out coherently for the first time. The conclusion of Part IV lives raw here.
sources.engagement: primary internal source the book draws from

sources.label: Amusing Ourselves to Death
sources.author: neil-postman
sources.summary: Argues that television as a medium degraded public discourse. The 'medium shapes message' thesis applied to a specific case.
sources.engagement: the book needs to know what it's adding past Postman
sources.file: Amusing Ourselves to Death Public Discourse in the Age of Show Business.pdf

sources.label: Not Born Yesterday
sources.author: hugo-mercier
sources.summary: Direct challenge to the 'people are easily manipulated by simple memes' thread. Humans have more robust epistemic vigilance than the easy-manipulation narrative implies.
sources.engagement: pressure-tests Chapter 7's emotional-memetics floor argument

sources.label: The Misinformation Age
sources.author: cailin-oconnor
sources.summary: Formal network models of belief propagation. What kills truth in networks: selection on credibility plus social pressure, not lossy hops.
sources.engagement: directly relevant to transport-vs-selection

sources.label: Echo Chambers and Epistemic Bubbles
sources.author: c-thi-nguyen
sources.summary: Distinguishes epistemic bubbles (missing info) from echo chambers (active discrediting of outside info). Small networks tend toward chambers.
sources.engagement: foundational for the rebuilt Part IV

sources.label: Understanding Media
sources.author: marshall-mcluhan
sources.summary: 'The medium is the message.' The canonical reference for how media shape what can pass through them.
sources.engagement: worth engaging explicitly

sources.label: The Selfish Gene
sources.author: richard-dawkins
sources.summary: Coined the term 'meme.' The selection-side view's foundational text.
sources.engagement: the selection-side view already has a literature; use it

sources.label: The Meme Machine
sources.author: susan-blackmore
sources.summary: Developed memetics into a sustained research program. Mechanisms of cultural selection.
sources.engagement: the selection-side view already has a literature; use it

sources.label: Nexus
sources.author: yuval-noah-harari
sources.summary: Information networks bound by myths and bureaucracy. Three realities (objective / subjective / intersubjective). Truth/order axis. Naive view of information.
sources.engagement: already in play; key framing reference

sources.label: Your Life in Weeks
sources.author: tim-urban
sources.summary: Tablespoon-of-diamonds visualization of a human lifespan. The receiver-budget intuition.
sources.engagement: cited as the source of the tablespoon-of-weeks framing

sources.label: An epidemiological approach to model viral propagation of memes
sources.summary: Models memetic propagation using epidemiological dynamics. Formal apparatus for the transport-stage math.
sources.engagement: candidate evidentiary source for Chapters 5 and 5b

sources.label: Information Evolution in Social Networks
sources.summary: Empirical work on how information morphs as it traverses social-media networks.
sources.engagement: candidate evidentiary source for the bridge-zone distortion case studies

sources.label: Memetics — a critique
sources.summary: Critical assessment of memetics as a research program. Where the analogy with genetic transmission breaks down.
sources.engagement: candidate pressure-tester for the selection-side framing

sources.label: Psychology of Virality
sources.summary: Empirical and theoretical work on what makes content go viral. Identity, emotion, in-group signaling.
sources.engagement: candidate evidentiary source for Chapters 5b and 7

sources.label: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
sources.author: douglas-hofstadter
sources.summary: Chapter VI, 'The Location of Meaning', develops the three-layer message model — frame (this is a message), outer (how to decode it), inner (what it means) — to ask whether meaning is intrinsic to a message or supplied by the decoder.
sources.engagement: source of the three-layer message model the book adapts

sources.label: Magnifica Humanitas (Encyclical of Pope Leo XIV)
sources.author: leo-xiv
sources.summary: May 2026 papal encyclical on artificial intelligence, technology, and the common good. Frames the choice as Babel (centralized, efficient, fragmenting) vs. Jerusalem (plural voices coordinated through shared responsibility). Distinguishes formal institutional power (state) from de facto power (tech/finance actors whose authority now exceeds many governments). Names the 'technocratic paradigm' as the ideology treating nature and humans as objects to dominate, and 'structures of sin' as institutionally-embedded systematic injustice. Calls for synodality (deliberative process across expertise domains) and an educational alliance for the digital age as counterforces.
sources.engagement: contemporary intervention on the book's themes; structurally aligned diagnosis with morally-philosophically grounded prescription; pressure-tests the book's prescriptive side on the polarization-via-distrust trap

sources.label: How to Ethically Build Public Good Infrastructure
sources.author: corey-petty
sources.summary: Devcon VI talk, October 2022. Applies Hofstadter's three-layer message model to infrastructure design — and makes the key move of identifying the outer message with the medium.
sources.engagement: primary internal source — first place the three-layer model was bound to the medium

sources.label: Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process
sources.author: rolf-landauer
sources.summary: Landauer (1961) established that erasing one bit of information carries an unavoidable thermodynamic cost of at least kT ln 2; Bennett (1982) used this to dissolve Maxwell's demon, showing the demon's apparent free order is paid back when it erases its memory. Grounds the book's 'a choice is a cost too' correction: aiming is never free, and the real split is blind cost vs. criterial cost.
sources.engagement: evidentiary grounding for the cost/choice asymmetry in Chapter 5b

sources.label: Selection and Covariance (the Price equation)
sources.author: george-price
sources.summary: Price (1970) decomposes the change in any trait across a generation into two terms: a selection term equal to the covariance between the trait and fitness, and a transmission term capturing everything imperfect transmission does. The aim lives entirely in the covariance; the transmission term is the blind cost, and biased (anisotropic) transmission sits there too — still un-steerable. Formal backing for the transport-as-cost / selection-as-choice split.
sources.engagement: evidentiary grounding for the two-term decomposition in Chapter 5b

sources.label: Mutations of Bacteria from Virus Sensitivity to Virus Resistance
sources.author: salvador-luria
sources.summary: Luria & Delbrück (1943), the fluctuation test: the wide variance in resistant-bacteria counts across parallel cultures showed mutations arise spontaneously before the selective pressure (the virus), not in adaptive response to it. Variation proposes blind, and only afterward does selection choose — grounding the book's claim that the generate step runs blind.
sources.engagement: evidentiary grounding for blind variation preceding selection in Chapter 5b

sources.label: The Construction of Social Reality
sources.author: john-searle
sources.summary: Institutional facts and status functions: X counts as Y in context C, sustained by collective intentionality. The canonical philosophical machinery for agreement-generated reality — would give the intersubjective-truth note's generator criterion its formal joints.
sources.engagement: not yet engaged; first-priority candidate for the intersubjective-truth thread

sources.label: Imagined Communities
sources.author: benedict-anderson
sources.summary: Nations as communities constituted through print capitalism — intersubjective constitution riding the same printing-press transition the book reads through the Hammer and Copernicus. Uncomfortably close to the intersubjective-truth note's instincts; engagement would sharpen or correct them.
sources.engagement: not yet engaged; candidate for the intersubjective-truth thread and the fork/secession material

sources.label: The Social Construction of Reality
sources.author: peter-berger
sources.summary: The founding text of the social-construction tradition: externalization, objectivation, internalization — a three-step account of how agreement hardens into experienced objectivity. Its 'objectivation' is the book's reification with sixty years of priority.
sources.engagement: not yet engaged; candidate — the objectivation/internalization ladder maps onto reification and trained-keys-are-shares

sources.label: The Social Construction of What?
sources.author: ian-hacking
sources.summary: Looping effects of human kinds: classifications change the people classified, who change the classification. The formal version of the self-fulfilling dynamics the intersubjective-truth note works through with bank runs.
sources.engagement: not yet engaged; candidate for the constitutive-volatility and self-fulfilling-loop material

sources.label: The Alchemy of Finance
sources.author: george-soros
sources.summary: Reflexivity: market participants' beliefs alter the fundamentals the beliefs are about. A practitioner's account of constitutive transmission in the one domain where it is priced daily.
sources.engagement: not yet engaged; candidate for the constitutive-volatility material

sources.label: Exit, Voice, and Loyalty
sources.author: albert-hirschman
sources.summary: The classic taxonomy of responses to institutional decline. Exit is the fork's economic theory; voice is renegotiation; loyalty is what delays both. Would give the fork-as-corrective argument its prior literature.
sources.engagement: not yet engaged; candidate for the fork-as-corrective and keep-the-fork-affordable material

sources.label: The Role of Deliberate Practice in the Acquisition of Expert Performance
sources.author: k-anders-ericsson
sources.summary: Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Römer, Psychological Review 100(3). Expert violinists' practice logs: about four hours a day of effortful practice was the sustainable ceiling; more led to exhaustion. The source of both Ch 3's focused-hours figure and, via Gladwell, the '10,000 hours' slogan.
sources.engagement: cited in Ch 3 for the focused-hours ceiling; the compression of this paper into '10,000 hours' is itself a worked example of the book's pipeline

sources.label: Categorization and Representation of Physics Problems by Experts and Novices
sources.author: michelene-chi
sources.summary: Chi, Feltovich & Glaser, Cognitive Science 5(2). Experts sort physics problems by the principle that solves them, novices by surface features. The classic evidence that prior structure changes what each hour of absorption can carry.
sources.engagement: cited in Ch 3 for the claim that receiver-budget capacity depends on structure already built

sources.label: Outliers
sources.author: malcolm-gladwell
sources.summary: Popular book whose '10,000-hour rule' compressed Ericsson et al. 1993 into a quantity claim the original authors rejected. Used in Ch 3 as a live example of a finding losing its decoding key in transit.
sources.engagement: cited in Ch 3 as an example, not as evidence

sources.label: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
sources.author: long-ouyang
sources.summary: The InstructGPT paper: reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) as the standard post-training method for aligning a model to human preference labels. In the book's terms, the training objective as a selection criterion lifted into the architecture.
sources.engagement: cited in Ch 11 for RLHF as objective-level selection (objective capture)

sources.label: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
sources.author: mrinank-sharma
sources.summary: Measures sycophancy: RLHF-tuned models systematically shift answers toward what the user appears to want rather than toward accuracy. Evidence that the reward favors the agreeable answer over the faithful one.
sources.engagement: cited in Ch 11 as evidence for objective capture (helpful/agreeable over faithful/corrective)

sources.label: AI Models Collapse When Trained on Recursively Generated Data
sources.author: ilia-shumailov
sources.summary: Model collapse: models trained on data produced by earlier models degrade across generations as the tails of the distribution are lost. The mechanism behind Ch 11's claim that objective capture is self-reinforcing across model generations.
sources.engagement: cited in Ch 11 for the self-reinforcing dynamic of objective capture and manufactured content in the training corpus

sources.label: Designing Organizations for an Information-Rich World
sources.author: herbert-simon
sources.summary: Origin of "a wealth of information creates a poverty of attention." Attention, not information, is the scarce resource once information is abundant.
sources.engagement: Bears on transport-collapse-shifts-constraint, the receiver budget (Ch 3), and cost-shifting (Ch 10). Supports: the founding statement that attention becomes the binding constraint. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: The Attention Merchants
sources.author: tim-wu
sources.summary: A 150-year history of the industries that harvest and resell human attention, from penny papers to social feeds.
sources.engagement: Bears on engagement-gates-reward-truth-loss and self-capture (Ch 10). Supports the engagement-as-business-model claim; pressure-tests the "no villain" framing with a long record of deliberate design. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism
sources.author: shoshana-zuboff
sources.summary: Behavioral surplus, prediction products, and the market that trades in them. The economic logic behind data-driven platforms.
sources.engagement: Bears on observation-cheap-defaults-breed-surveillance and captured-generator-decides-truth. Supports the industry claim; pressure-tests the "default, not choice" framing by arguing the surveillance is engineered. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: The Communication Structure of Epistemic Communities
sources.author: kevin-zollman
sources.summary: Formal models showing that denser communication among inquirers can lower a community's accuracy (the Zollman effect); with "The Epistemic Benefit of Transient Diversity" (Erkenntnis, 2010) on why premature consensus hurts.
sources.engagement: Bears on Chapter 9's Zollman effect (currently cited only via O'Connor & Weatherall) and integration-needs-agent-and-infrastructure. Supports: the primary source for a load-bearing borrowed result. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: How Behavior Spreads / The Spread of Behavior in an Online Social Network Experiment
sources.author: damon-centola
sources.summary: Complex contagions (costly or controversial behaviors) need reinforcement from multiple contacts to spread, unlike simple contagions. Includes the 2010 Science online-network experiment.
sources.engagement: Bears on complexity-virality-inverse, complexity-ceiling-by-network-size, and Chapter 9's sparse-bridges prescription. Supports the complexity/spread inverse; pressure-tests "bridges sparse enough" — complex ideas need wide, redundant bridges, not thin ones. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Experimental evidence for scale-induced category convergence across populations
sources.author: douglas-guilbeault
sources.summary: Larger populations independently converge on the same category systems; scale drives convergence rather than fragmentation.
sources.engagement: Bears on compression-widens-latitude and myth-reach-determinacy-tradeoff. Pressure-tests: scale produces convergence of categories, the reverse sign of the dilution loop, which the book must answer. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: The spread of true and false news online
sources.author: soroush-vosoughi
sources.summary: A study of ~126,000 cascades on Twitter: false news spread farther, faster, and more broadly than true news, driven by novelty and by emotions of surprise and disgust.
sources.engagement: Bears on engagement-gates-reward-truth-loss, selection-picks-the-regime, and engagement-floor-of-raw-emotion. Supports (falsehood diffuses farther/faster; novelty plus surprise and disgust); pressure-tests the gate locus, since humans, not bots, did the spreading. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Emotion shapes the diffusion of moralized content in social networks
sources.author: william-brady
sources.summary: Each moral-emotional word in a message raised its retweet rate, and diffusion stayed largely within ideological in-groups.
sources.engagement: Bears on engagement-floor-of-raw-emotion, floor-is-aggregation-property, and the unify-and-fragment dynamic. Supports: moral-emotional language raises spread and stays in-group. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Greater Internet use is not associated with faster growth in political polarization among US demographic groups
sources.author: levi-boxell
sources.summary: Across US demographic groups, polarization grew fastest among those least likely to use the internet and social media.
sources.engagement: Bears on timescale-distinction-mercier-book and the generational form of the engagement floor. Pressure-tests: the cohort with least exposure polarized fastest, against a simple medium-causes-polarization story. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: How do social media feed algorithms affect attitudes and behavior in an election campaign?
sources.author: andrew-guess
sources.summary: A 2020-election field experiment: switching users from algorithmic to chronological feeds changed exposure but not downstream attitudes over three months.
sources.engagement: Bears on adding-channel-can-accelerate-divergence, timescale-distinction, and medium-attached-to-every-gate. Pressure-tests short-run gate-tuning effects; read correctly it supports the timescale distinction, since three-month nulls say nothing about decades. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Like-minded sources on Facebook are prevalent but not polarizing
sources.author: brendan-nyhan
sources.summary: Reducing exposure to like-minded sources on Facebook did not measurably change polarization over the study window.
sources.engagement: Bears on adding-channel-can-accelerate-divergence and the timescale-distinction. Pressure-tests short-run effects; supports the timescale distinction that short experiments cannot settle long-run dynamics. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Shifting attention to accuracy can reduce misinformation online
sources.author: gordon-pennycook
sources.summary: People share misinformation partly because attention is on engagement, not accuracy; a simple accuracy prompt improved sharing quality. With "Lazy, not biased" (Cognition, 2019) on analytic thinking.
sources.engagement: Bears on demand-side-filter-on-integration and floor-is-aggregation-property. Supports the preference/sharing disconnect; pressure-tests the justification-market reading, since the driver may be inattention rather than motivation. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Rethinking Expertise
sources.author: harry-collins
sources.summary: A taxonomy of expertise, including interactional expertise: fluency in a field's language acquired without contributory practice.
sources.engagement: Bears on bridge-node-is-versatile-specialist and Chapter 8's tacit-knowledge argument. Pressure-tests: interactional expertise can bridge without contributory depth; supports the training-function claim that tacit knowledge needs apprenticeship. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Governing the Commons
sources.author: elinor-ostrom
sources.summary: Design principles for durable common-pool-resource institutions: clear boundaries, monitoring, graduated sanctions, nested governance, low-cost exit.
sources.engagement: Bears on loop-outcome-set-by-capture-resistance and Chapter 12's design principles. Supports: the prior literature on capture-resistant institutional design the chapter reinvents. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Seeing Like a State
sources.author: james-scott
sources.summary: How states impose legibility by simplifying complex local reality, and how high-modernist simplification fails.
sources.engagement: Bears on bureaucracy-downstream-of-myth and Chapter 8. Pressure-tests: bureaucracy as the compressor (legibility) rather than the key-restorer, which the book's narrow stipulation must answer. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: The Expanding News Desert
sources.author: penelope-abernathy
sources.summary: Documented the closure of more than 2,000 US newspapers since 2005, with the Medill State of Local News reports (2022- ) continuing the count.
sources.engagement: Bears on Chapter 10's local-journalism-collapse claim and the "preservation mostly held" softening. Supports with numbers: the measured scale of local-news collapse. Quote-backed supports/pressureTests edges pending extraction of the source PDF

sources.label: Intuitive and Reflective Beliefs
sources.author: dan-sperber
sources.summary: Sperber's distinction between intuitive beliefs (wired into one's other beliefs, driving action) and reflective beliefs (held at arm's length, stated and shared but often inert in action). Chapter 7's account of what the floor spreads rests on it: most alarming material is forwarded as a reflective belief, a coalition-marker, not an intuitive one that moves behavior.
sources.engagement: Cited in Ch 7 for the reflective/intuitive split that explains why people share things they never act on. Page-level quote verification pending the source text.
